lines.founded: The {trade} of {town} found {name}, meeting at {hall}. They choose {master} as guild master{backing}.
lines.backing: , and the guild will lean on {councillor} the {seat} at the council
lines.master: {name} has a new guild master: {master}, who works at {hall}.
lines.backs: {name} takes {councillor} the {seat} to dinner. The guild will back them at the council.
lines.demand: {master}, master of {name}, comes to the town hall: the guild wants {want}, and gives the mayor {days} days.
lines.met: {name} has what it asked for. {master} thanks the mayor before the whole guild.
lines.lapsed: The days {name} gave the mayor run out without {want}. {master} tells the guild the town hall does not listen.
lines.crossed: {name} takes it ill that the mayor {ruling}.
lines.strike: {name} goes on strike: from {hall} to the last {member}, its people down tools until the town hall listens. {master} speaks for them.
lines.ends: The strike of {name} ends. Its people go back to work for want of wages, sullen.
lines.paid: The mayor pays {name} {gold} gold to drop the matter. {master} counts it twice.
lines.broken: The watch breaks the strike of {name}: {master}'s pickets are pulled from the doors of {hall} and the guild is sent back to work. The town remembers it.

union._doc: The guilds against the mages (Systems/Union.cs): a bar from -100 (the guilds have the town hall's ear) to +100 (the mages do). It drifts toward where the town's doings pull it: research funding, hedge mages, the wizards' library, the Unshut Book and wizards toward the mages; each guild and their good temper back. Near the middle (concord) both work together; past lean the slighted side grumbles; past breaking it acts every breakEvery days. Hearing a side out moves it hearShift; taking a side holds the bar at the end for sideDays, with consequences, and leaves a grudge.

lines.formed: The masters of {guilds} meet behind closed doors and come out as one: the union of {town}'s trades. Every spell cast for wages, they say, is bread out of a worker's mouth, and the town hall had better remember it.
lines.grumble: The union grumbles that the town hall has eyes only for its mages. Guild halls are full of angry talk, and the guilds' temper sours by the day.
lines.sulk: The mages say the town hall listens only to the guilds. The library's lamps burn late less often, and its studies slow.
lines.concord: The guilds and the mages of {town} have found an uneasy peace: the masons hire a builder-mage now and then, and the library buys its ink from the drapers.
lines.march: The union marches on the town hall with torches and hammers: every guild in {town} downs tools together until the mayor stops favouring the mages.
lines.walkout: The mages of {town} walk out of the library, saying the town hall listens only to the guilds. {wizard}
lines.hearGuilds: The mayor sits with the union's masters for a long evening and pays {cost} gold toward their grievances.
lines.hearMages: The mayor dines with the town's mages and pays {cost} gold for new lamps, ink and a stipend.
lines.sideGuilds: The mayor sides with the union: hedge magic is banned from the trades, and {hedge} hedge mages put their spells away. The guilds cheer. The mages do not forget.
lines.sideMages: The mayor sides with the mages: magic will be welcome in every trade in {town}. The union takes it as a declaration of war, and the guild halls empty into the streets.
lines.lapsed: A season on, the town hall's favour is no longer fixed. The guilds and the mages are back to haggling for it, and the slighted side has not forgotten.

guilds.name: the Company of Masons and Wrights
guilds.strike: Scaffolds stand empty and no stone or timber reaches the sites.

guilds.name: the Hammer and Tongs
guilds.strike: The forges go cold and no tools reach the market.

wants.text: {amount} more watchmen, armed from their forges

guilds.name: the Fellowship of Brewers and Innkeepers
guilds.strike: The taps run dry and the taverns bar their doors.

wants.text: a feast day for the town, the ale bought on the council's coin

guilds.name: the Tillers' and Millers' Guild
guilds.strike: The fields go untended and the carts stop coming to market.

guilds.name: the Drapers' and Chandlers' Company
guilds.strike: Shutters stay down along the market and the looms stand still.

wants.text: a market fair, paid for by the council
